title: Thanksgiving storm knocks out power, disrupts flights on US East Coast
html:
A storm in New York on Nov 26. The storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast.

PHOTO: REUTERS

AI generated

WASHINGTON – A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast on Nov 26, knocking out power to nearly one million customers at one point as wind gusts of up to 112kmh toppled trees and power lines.

Storms contributed to flight delays, with FlightAware reporting a total of 454 US-related cancellations on Nov 26 and 2,411 delays.

Major airports in the Washington and New York City areas were among the hardest hit.

Heavy rain flooded coastal areas, while utilities warned that rain-soaked ground and strong winds could increase the risk of falling trees and power outages.

More than 908,000 US utility customers had no power as at 9.56pm Eastern time (10.56am in Singapore on Nov 27), according to PowerOutage.us, down from 961,000 at 7.30pm ET.

The data included more than 207,000 outages in Pennsylvania, over 179,000 in New Jersey, 139,000 in Maryland, 106,000 in Virginia, 100,000 in Missouri and more than 68,000 in New York state.

Utilities and state officials had warned the combination of strong onshore winds and rain could cause widespread power disruptions.

Wind gusts of 80 to 112kmh were reported or forecast across parts of Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and coastal New England, according to the US National Weather Service (NWS).

It said conditions would gradually improve across the Mid-Atlantic overnight as the heaviest rain and strongest winds moved into New England, although blustery conditions with gusts of 40-56kmh were expected across parts of the East Coast on Nov 27.

New York City Emergency Management reported winds intensified on Nov 26 afternoon, reaching 90kmh at LaGuardia Airport.

The NWS said strong onshore winds associated with the storm, combined with king tides, were causing coastal flooding in low-lying communities along portions of the East Coast.

The threat of storms had already led officials to postpone Nov 26’s 100th edition of the annual Macy’s ​Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City, marking the first time the event has been rescheduled due to severe weather.

Separately on Nov 26, US President Donald Trump said he had approved about US$100 million (S$129 million) in federal aid to Florida following severe storms and flooding there.

He said the total included funding previously approved in connection with Hurricane Isaias in October. REUTERS
summary: More than 836,000 US utility customers had no power.
